resources.name: Jamaica Bay-Rockaway Parks Conservancy
resources.address: 11404 Beach Channel Drive, Rockaway Park, NY 11694
resources.mission: Jamaica Bay is New York City's largest and most ecologically productive open space - an unparalleled oasis of nature covering 44 square miles of open water, tidal wetlands, and coastal parklands altogether twice the size of Manhattan - that directly serves more than 1 million New Yorkers who live in adjacent Queens and Brooklyn neighborhoods and more than 3 million who live within its watershed. As a unique public-private partnership that works across city, state and federal agencies, Jamaica Bay-Rockaway Parks Conservancy (JBRPC) was established in 2013 to bring together diverse community stakeholders, elected officials, academic researchers and others toward a common goal: improving public parklands for enjoyment and ecosystem health. Since our founding in 2013, JBRPC has removed nearly 55 tons of trash and debris from shorelines and parks, planted more than 425,000 native plants and trees, hosted more than 125,000 people at public programs and events, organized more than 200 stewardship events that drew support from 4,000 dedicated volunteers, and welcomed 17,000 students into our environmental education programs.
